minutes.headline: Committee voted by roll call to suspend Test and Stay and move to symptomatic COVID testing with at-home kits.
minutes.summary: An emergency special meeting heard the superintendent's recommendation to drop Test and Stay and contact tracing and adopt symptomatic testing with weekly at-home rapid kits from the state. Members asked about asymptomatic people, consent, unions, and nursing staff views. The motion was moved, seconded and taken by roll call, then the meeting adjourned.

public_comment.topic: A union representative thanked the nurses and committee, said the state's offer of rapid tests is what the unions had asked for, and praised the state for helping ease pressure on nurses.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted by roll call to suspend Test and Stay and move to symptomatic testing of students and staff; all four members heard voted yes.
The superintendent's recommendation was to drop Test and Stay and contact tracing and use weekly at-home rapid kits supplied by the state.
Members asked about consent, asymptomatic people, unions, nursing staff and younger students before the motion was taken.
A union representative said the state's offer of rapid tests is what the unions had asked for and that it eases pressure on nurses.
Administration said it will push notification to staff and families once the testing materials are ready.

why_it_matters: This changes how COVID exposure is handled in the schools for families and staff: testing now begins with symptoms and at-home kits rather than testing in school after an exposure.
No budget item was voted, and the minutes record no local cost; the kits come from the state.
watch_next: Notice from administration to staff and families once the testing materials are ready.
